## Overview – A restaurant website must be functional, GST‑ready and display the FSSAI licence before it goes live.  
A launch checklist helps you verify that every technical, legal and user‑experience element is in place, so you avoid costly rework after the site is public.

Govindani Infotech Pvt. Ltd. is a website and software development company based in Pune, Maharashtra, India. For restaurants that need a reliable partner, we often start with a clear, step‑by‑step plan that covers everything from domain registration to compliance banners. Below is a detailed checklist designed for Pune‑based eateries that must comply with GST and FSSAI regulations while offering smooth digital payments such as UPI.

### Why a checklist matters for Indian restaurants  
A checklist reduces the risk of missing a legal requirement (e.g., displaying the FSSAI licence) or a technical detail (e.g., GST‑compliant invoice generation). Missing any of these can lead to GST penalties, FSSAI notices, or loss of customer trust.

---

## Domain and Hosting – Secure a reliable address and server before you start building.  
Choosing the right domain name and hosting plan sets the foundation for performance, SEO and compliance.

### 1. Choose a domain that reflects your brand and is easy to type  
- Keep it short, preferably .in or .com.  
- Include the restaurant name; avoid hyphens and numbers that can be misread.  
- Register the domain through an accredited Indian registrar (e.g., GoDaddy India, BigRock) to ensure local support and GST invoicing.

### 2. Select a hosting provider that offers Indian data centre locations  
- A server in Mumbai or Pune reduces latency for local users.  
- Look for providers that support SSL certificates, daily backups and 24 × 7 support.  
- Ensure the hosting plan includes enough bandwidth for image‑heavy menus and occasional traffic spikes during festivals.

### 3. Enable HTTPS with a valid SSL certificate  
- HTTPS encrypts data, which is mandatory for any site that collects payment information.  
- Most hosts include a free Let’s Encrypt certificate; you can also purchase an EV SSL for added brand trust.

### 4. Set up DNS and point it to your hosting IP  
- Use the registrar’s DNS management panel to add A records (for the main domain) and CNAME records (for www).  
- Add a TXT record for SPF/DKIM if you plan to send newsletters from the same domain.

---

## Design and Content – Build a user‑friendly site that showcases the menu and brand identity.  
A well‑structured site improves conversion and makes compliance elements easier to place.

### 1. Define the site architecture  
- Typical pages: Home, About, Menu, Order Online, Gallery, Contact, Legal (GST & FSSAI).  
- Use a flat hierarchy (no more than three clicks to any page) to aid both users and search engines.

### 2. Upload a high‑quality, searchable menu  
- Use structured data (Schema.org `Menu` markup) so Google can display dishes in search results.  
- Include dish names, descriptions, allergens, and prices in INR.  
- Keep the menu in a CMS (e.g., WordPress, Strapi) so you can update it without developer help.

### 3. Ensure mobile‑first responsiveness  
- Over 70 % of restaurant searches in India happen on mobile devices.  
- Test breakpoints for 320 px, 480 px, and 768 px using Chrome DevTools.  

### 4. Add brand elements and local SEO signals  
- Include the restaurant’s name, address, and phone number in the footer using `LocalBusiness` schema.  
- Embed a Google Map of the Pune location; this helps with “near me” searches.

### 5. Write clear call‑to‑actions (CTAs) for ordering and reservations  
- Use action verbs (“Order Now”, “Book a Table”) and place them above the fold.  
- Link CTAs to the payment gateway or reservation system with UPI integration (see next section).

---

## Payment Integration – Enable UPI, cards and wallets while keeping GST compliance.  
A seamless checkout reduces cart abandonment and ensures every transaction is recorded for tax purposes.

### 1. Choose a payment gateway that supports UPI and Indian cards  
| Feature | Razorpay | PayU | Instamojo |
|---|---|---|---|
| UPI support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| GST invoice auto‑generation | ✅ (via API) | ✅ (via webhook) | ❌ (requires custom code) |
| Settlement time | 2‑3 business days | 2‑4 business days | 3‑5 business days |
| Indian support desk | 24 × 7 | 24 × 7 | Business hours only |

- All three gateways are PCI‑DSS compliant, which satisfies card‑payment security requirements.  
- For restaurants that want the simplest integration, Razorpay’s SDK works well with most CMS platforms.

### 2. Implement the gateway’s SDK or API  
- Follow the provider’s documentation to embed the checkout widget on the “Order Online” page.  
- Test in sandbox mode before switching to live credentials.  

### 3. Capture the payer’s name, phone number and email  
- These fields are required for GST invoicing and for sending order confirmations.  
- Store the data securely (see Security section).

### 4. Configure automatic GST‑ready invoices  
- Enable the gateway’s “tax” module and set the GST rate (currently 5 % or 12 % for restaurant services, depending on the menu).  
- The generated PDF should display the restaurant’s GSTIN, invoice number, and taxable value.  

### 5. Display a “Pay via UPI” QR code for dine‑in orders (optional)  
- Generate a static UPI QR using your VPA (e.g., restaurant@upi).  
- Place the QR on the checkout page and optionally on printed receipts.

---

## GST‑Ready Billing – Ensure every online sale produces a compliant invoice.  
GST compliance is mandatory for any restaurant with annual turnover above the exemption limit; even small eateries benefit from proper invoicing.

### 1. Register for GST and obtain a GSTIN  
- Apply through the GST portal (https://www.gst.gov.in).  
- Keep the GST registration certificate handy; you’ll need to display the GSTIN on the site.

### 2. Add GST details to the website footer and checkout pages  
- Example footer line: “GSTIN: 27AAEPM1234F1Z5”.  
- Show the applicable tax rate next to each menu price (e.g., “₹250 + GST”).

### 3. Choose an invoicing method that integrates with your payment gateway  
- Options: built‑in gateway invoicing, third‑party API (e.g., ClearTax, Zoho Books), or custom PDF generation.  
- The invoice must contain: GSTIN of the restaurant, GSTIN of the buyer (if B2B), invoice number, date, itemised list, tax amount, and total.

### 4. Store invoices for the statutory period (minimum 6 years)  
- Use a cloud storage bucket (e.g., AWS S3, Google Cloud) with proper folder naming (year/month).  
- Ensure backups are encrypted and comply with Indian data‑privacy norms.

### 5. Enable “Download Invoice” for customers after payment  
- Provide a secure link that expires after 30 days for security.  
- Include a “Print” button that triggers the PDF view.

---

## FSSAI Licence Display – Show the food‑safety licence prominently to satisfy regulators.  
FSSAI compliance is a legal requirement for any restaurant that sells food, and the licence must be visible to customers.

### 1. Locate your FSSAI licence number and certificate  
- The licence number appears on the certificate (e.g., “FSSAI/1234/2022”).  
- Keep a digital copy (PDF) for uploading to the website.

### 2. Add a “Food Safety” badge in the footer or on the “About” page  
- Use the official FSSAI logo (available on the FSSAI website) and link it to the licence PDF.  
- Example text: “FSSAI Licence No. 1234‑2022 – Valid till 31 Dec 2025”.

### 3. Include the licence information in the website’s “Legal” page  
- Provide the full address of the registered kitchen, the licence number, and the expiry date.  
- This page can be linked from the footer with anchor text “Legal & Compliance”.

### 4. Keep the licence PDF updated before expiry  
- Set a calendar reminder three months before the licence renewal date.  
- Replace the PDF and update the expiry date on the site to avoid non‑compliance notices.

---

## Analytics, SEO and Performance – Track visitors, rank locally and keep the site fast.  
Performance and discoverability directly affect online orders, especially for new restaurants in Pune.

### 1. Install Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with consent mode  
- Add the GA4 tag via Google Tag Manager for easier management.  
- Enable consent mode to respect Indian privacy expectations (no intrusive tracking before user consent).

### 2. Set up Google Search Console for the domain  
- Verify ownership using the DNS TXT record.  
- Submit the XML sitemap (generated by your CMS) to help Google crawl menu pages.

### 3. Implement local SEO best practices  
- Use `LocalBusiness` schema with fields: name, address, telephone, opening hours, cuisine type.  
- Register the restaurant on Google My Business (now “Google Business Profile”) with accurate address, photos and operating hours.

### 4. Optimize images for speed  
- Compress menu photos using WebP format (target < 150 KB per image).  
- Serve images via a CDN that has PoPs in India (e.g., Cloudflare, Akamai).

### 5. Test page load time with Google PageSpeed Insights  
- Aim for a First Contentful Paint (FCP) under 2 seconds on a 4G connection typical in Pune.  
- Address suggestions such as “Eliminate render‑blocking resources” and “Serve images in next‑gen format”.

---

## Security, Backups and Privacy – Protect customer data and stay within Indian regulations.  
A breach can damage reputation and attract penalties under the Information Technology (IT) Act.

### 1. Harden the CMS and plugins  
- Keep core, themes and plugins updated; remove any unused extensions.  
- Use a security plugin that limits login attempts and monitors file changes.

### 2. Implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF)  
- Many Indian hosts provide a built‑in WAF; enable rules for SQL injection, XSS and bad bots.  

### 3. Encrypt data at rest and in transit  
- SSL/TLS already covers data in transit.  
- For stored customer details (phone, email, order history), enable server‑side encryption (e.g., AES‑256).

### 4. Draft a privacy policy compliant with Indian law  
- Mention data collection purposes (order processing, marketing), retention period, and user rights.  
- Include a link to the policy in the footer and on the checkout page.

### 5. Schedule automated backups  
- Daily incremental backups and weekly full backups stored in a separate region (e.g., Mumbai → Singapore) protect against ransomware.  
- Test restoration at least once a quarter.

---

## Launch Checklist – Verify every item before you point the domain to production.  
A final verification step saves you from post‑launch firefighting.

| Category | Task | Done? |
|---|---|---|
| Domain & Hosting | Register domain, set DNS, enable SSL | ☐ |
| Design | Mobile‑responsive layout, menu uploaded, schema markup | ☐ |
| Payments | UPI & card gateway integrated, sandbox tested, live credentials set | ☐ |
| GST | GSTIN displayed, tax rates configured, invoice generation tested | ☐ |
| FSSAI | Licence number shown, PDF linked, expiry date current | ☐ |
| Analytics | GA4 tag, consent banner, Search Console verified | ☐ |
| SEO | LocalBusiness schema, Google Business Profile claimed | ☐ |
| Performance | Images optimized, CDN active, PageSpeed > 80 | ☐ |
| Security | SSL active, WAF enabled, backups scheduled, privacy policy live | ☐ |
| Legal | Terms of Service, Refund policy, cookie consent | ☐ |

Walk through the table row by row, marking each checkbox only after you have verified the corresponding item on a staging environment.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions  

### How do I display my GSTIN on the website without violating privacy?  
Place the GSTIN in the site footer and on the checkout page where tax calculations occur. It is a public identifier, so no privacy concern arises, but avoid exposing the full PAN of the business.

### Which payment gateway offers the simplest UPI integration for a small restaurant?  
Razorpay provides a ready‑to‑use UPI button and a JavaScript SDK that works with most Indian CMS platforms. Its sandbox environment lets you test transactions without a live account.

### Do I need a separate SSL certificate for each sub‑domain (e.g., order.restaurant.com)?  
A single wildcard SSL (e.g., `*.restaurant.com`) covers all sub‑domains and is cheaper than buying individual certificates. Ensure the wildcard is issued by a reputable CA.

### How often should I update my menu on the website?  
Update the menu whenever there is a price change, new dish addition, or seasonal item removal. Using a CMS allows you to edit content instantly without developer involvement.

### What are the penalties for not showing the FSSAI licence on the site?  
The FSSAI can issue a show‑cause notice, and repeated non‑compliance may lead to fines ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹50,000, depending on the severity and duration of the violation.

### Can I use a free website builder for my restaurant and still stay GST‑compliant?  
Free builders may lack integration with GST‑ready invoicing APIs. If you need automatic tax calculations and downloadable invoices, choose a platform that supports custom code or a paid plan that offers these features.

---

## Where to Start  

1. Register your domain and set up a reliable Indian host with SSL.  
2. Obtain GST registration and FSSAI licence if not already done.  
3. Choose a payment gateway (Razorpay, PayU or Instamojo) and configure UPI.  
4. Install a CMS, upload the menu with structured data, and add GST/FSSAI details.  
5. Run the launch checklist table, fix any red flags, and go live.
